newsitem.title: USA: Report warns of resurgence of yellow fever.
newsitem.headline: Report warns of resurgence of yellow fever.

text.p: There has been a dramatic reemergence of yellow fever in Africa and Latin America since the 1980s, threatening outbreaks in the United States for the first time in decades, researchers said on Tuesday.

Because a mosquito that carries the disease has again established itself in urban areas in the two regions "there is widespread concern that yellow fever could erupt in explosive outbreaks, which could also occur in the southeastern United States," the report from the World Health Organization said.
The disease has not been reported in North America since 1905 when an outbreak in New Orleans infected 5,000 people, killing 1,000 of them.

"But in recent years much of the southern United States has been reinfested with (the mosquito) and a yellow fever outbreak could occur," said the report published in this week's Journal of the American Medical Association.

About 15 percent of people bitten by infected mosquitos develop serious cases of the fever. In many of those the disease reaches a toxic phase which can be fatal. The disease is currently found only in Central and South America and a large portion of Africa.
Vaccine to prevent infection is commonly used by international travelers but only a small proportion at-risk residents of many developing countries are vaccinated because of the cost, the study said.

Between 1987 and 1991 there were 18,735 cases of the fever reported, the largest amount in any five-year period since 1948, the article said. During 1994 and 1995 outbreaks were reported in Cameroon, Ghana, Liberia, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Gabon and Kenya, and in 1995 Peru suffered the largest outbreak reported from any South American country since 1950, the study said.
